speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the current take-up rate of the SkillsFuture Credit (SFC) for lifelong learning and training in the workforce; (b) how responsive have senior citizens and back-to-work women been in utilising their SFC for training and retraining; and (c) whether there are any problems that workers have highlighted in accessing their SFC.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) as of 2023, how many eligible Singaporeans have fully utilised their SkillsFuture credits; (b) whether the SkillsFuture credits can be replenished for those who have used up their credits; and (c) what are the reasons why 70% of eligible individuals have not been utilising their SkillsFuture credits since 2015.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The SkillsFuture Credit (SFC) empowers Singaporeans to take ownership of their learning and also skills development.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The SFC, we all know, can be used to offset the fees for a wide range of skills-related courses, after Government course fee subsidies are applied.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Only a small minority of Singaporeans have fully expended their SFC.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: These individuals can continue to enjoy substantial course fee subsidies of up to 90% provided by the Government.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: This is an annual increase of around 12,000 per year, from 156,000 in 2019.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: This growth has been supported by efforts of SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and its partners to promote a culture of lifelong learning and help individuals to make informed choices, based on their training needs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: These partners include the trade unions, enterprises, Community Development Councils (CDCs), trade associations and professional bodies.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For example, SSG works closely with these partners to expand the provision of skills and training advisory services at job fairs, workshops, community events and touchpoints across the island.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Specific to older Singaporeans, SSG works with partner agencies to ensure that there is a suitable range of SFC-eligible courses to cater to their upskilling and lifelong learning needs, such as digital literacy, financial literacy and physical and mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: There are also longer courses under the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme that incorporate career coaching and employment facilitation services.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: This is to help the trainees secure employment upon completion of these upskilling courses.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: To further improve SFC utilisation, SSG has enhanced the user experience of mySkillsFuture portal, making it easier for users to navigate and search for suitable SFC courses for themselves.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: SSG has also simplified the claims submission process, based on users' feedback.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: In addition, to keep the courses relevant to the industry, SSG works closely with industry partners and regularly analyses data on job vacancies and skills in demand.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: More details will be announced later this year.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: First is that, is the Government happy with the state of affairs of the current SFC utilisation?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is 50% of the of the population using SFC the target?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Is there a near-term three years or five years target of raising this even higher?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Second, for eligible Singaporeans, is there any way to encourage the remaining 50% on how they can use their SFC?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What is the reason why they are not using it now, currently?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Can the Ministry look into how to use AI or other methods to suggest courses for Singaporeans as well as identify skills or courses that they may take up?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: So, prompt them, push them a little bit, so that they can use this important fund to help improve their lives.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: First, is on whether we are happy with the state of the utilisation of SFC?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I would say that we have seen good progress over the years.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Especially since the launch of SFC, we see more Singaporeans understanding the needs of lifelong learning and upskilling; and employers too, seeing the benefit of upskilling their workers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I would say that we know we are on the right trajectory.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: What is more important is that skills development and training are available and relevant, where the individuals need them.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is not limited to the use of SFC.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Although SFC is a key pillar in this ecosystem, we know that employers too, also play a big role in shaping and supporting their workers and their new hires in upskilling.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: There are also, of course, free courses online that are widely available and that are very popular.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, the utilisation of SFC is a proxy, I would say.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We are moving in the right direction and we welcome suggestions by members of public, as well as Members in this Chamber, on what else we can do to improve the utilisation.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: On why some Singaporeans might not be using SFC, some have cited lack of time and some have cited opportunity costs when they go for upskilling.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, we hope that the upcoming announcements for us to enhance SFC, as well as training allowance, will help more Singaporeans take the big step to go for upskilling.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My first question is, whether this new push in SFC, is there any change in emphasis, or any new emphasis?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Is this like a version two of SFC that we are expecting?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And secondly, the Minister of State mentioned about working with professional bodies.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I thought it is a very good idea because they are more attuned to the changes, the professionals skill needs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And so, whether under the new push, are we going to work more closely with the professional bodies?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is not a programme; by that, I mean it takes many parties to come together for this movement to create impact on individuals.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We are glad that professional bodies are also coming onboard.
